_what_this_is: The exact Snap/Bitmoji renderer recipe for Crid, the character in the desk overlay. Use it to render more poses and weight stages of the SAME avatar. It is not a license to design a new character. The recipe is the owner's own avatar URL (fetch-crid-views.mjs in the CRID archive) with two deliberate changes: `body` is filled per stage, and `bag=-1` removes the backpack — the bag is a prop the overlay draws, not part of his render.
_endpoint_warning: Do NOT use avatar-builder-v3/preview/body for Crid. That endpoint ignores the outfit params and renders Snap's minimum clothing — a white undershirt and white briefs — which is not his look. bm-preview honours the full recipe: bare chest (clothing_type=1), camo trousers (bottom=10001984), socks, shoes. Snap has no nude render; bare chest + his own kit is the floor.
_derivation: The exact user-selected body-000-r7.webp is the production leanest image and canonical face source. Its original bytes are retained for body-3-r0.webp. Six heavier Snap body renders use the same face crop copied from that reference; the backpack stays separate. Historical r7 widths define the seven silhouette targets.
_rules: BARE CHEST, HIS OWN KIT — no shirt, no straps, no backpack in the render (bag=-1). He wears the recipe's camo trousers, socks and shoes. Accessories and the backpack are separate objects the overlay draws.
rotation MUST be 0. Crid is drawn front-facing. rotation=7 (three-quarter) is what made earlier weight stages look like different people.

The seven production keys are 3, 0, 4, 5, 1, 11, 2 (leanest -> heaviest). Key 3 is the exact archived body-000-r7.webp reference, not a fresh Snap render. The six heavier builds use Snap body values 0, 4, 5, 1, 11 and 2 at rotation 0; do not invent stage numbers the renderer does not produce.

The exact body-000-r7.webp image is the leanest production render (307 px visible-ink width, 1156 px visible-ink height, floor y=1325). Visible ink excludes alpha fringe at or below 8. Its head/face pixels are copied exactly into every heavier stage. All stages retain the same measured 1156 px ink height; only horizontal body width and mass change.

The six heavier body stages are fetched at rotation 0, translated to the reference torso axis and floor, and receive the exact r7 head crop. Horizontal body-only deformation creates the historical width ladder; the leanest stage is never regenerated or resampled.
Never pass these parameters to an image-generation model. They belong to Snap's renderer and nowhere else.
Tone values must be sent as DECIMAL integers. Hex strings in a URL make the renderer answer HTTP 400 with an empty body.

body_stages.2: heaviest (belly, thicker limbs — same measured height and head as every other stage)

rigs: scripts/build-crid-rig.py --all cuts public/desk-assets/crid/rigs/<stage>/ from each stage's own frame — ten pieces plus rig.json per stage, aggregated into public/desk-assets/crid/rig.mjs (RIGS keyed by stage).

face_reference.description: User-selected neutral, closed-mouth face and lean-silhouette reference; the old rotated companion frames are not production poses.
